steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone openai/codex at cb00a675 (not 2f5e242) and confirm the commit matches rust-v0.163.0.
Grep codex-rs for service_tier, service-tier and fast_mode in protocol, app-server-protocol, config and core to see what the base already has.
Check whether the base already carries the upstream #13212/#13334 plumbing; if it does, the task premise fails and the start is non-zero.
Run cargo build of the codex-rs workspace (or the cli and app-server crates) with a timer, offline after fetch, to measure real build cost and RAM.
Run the existing workspace tests for config and app-server protocol to see whether they pass and how long they take.
Ask whether an upstream commit with the feature exists after cb00a675 (later release or PR) and record its SHA.
Do not write a reference; if steps 2 and 3 show the feature is already present, stop and kill.

v1.summary: The seed asks for service tier support in Codex CLI and app-server at cb00a675, but public upstream commits (#13212, #13334) from March 2026 already implement the feature, so the base may not start from zero and the reference is recallable (K11). The smoke build is amber, ran a node build instead of cargo, and listed no tests, and its commit (2f5e242) does not match the pinned head (cb00a675); the spike should first check whether the base already contains the feature.
